entries.32cce6de049ecd10: In its medium-term 3-year management plan starting in fiscal 2024, the company is working on building a stable business portfolio with growth potential, in order to proactively respond to future changes in the management environment. The business model it aims for is a "long-term cyclical business that realizes sustainable growth through synergies among businesses centered on transportation and real estate and through reinvestment," and it positions the 3 years of the plan as a period of restart. Its priority measures are 3: internal growth through improvement of the earning power of existing businesses (achieving both provision of social value through "movement" and profitability, and value-up investment and collaboration among businesses); continuation of growth investment for sustainable growth (improvement of area value through real estate development, expansion of the real estate sales business, continued promotion of overseas business, and GX investment); and strengthening of the consolidated management and business promotion base (human resource strategy and digital strategy). Its vision word is "Creative Act.: With creativity, flexibly, 'a town the world longs for.'"

entries.70fe91f235e9afad: This reportable segment operates department store, chain store, shopping center, credit card, cable television, advertising and video businesses. The company positions this business as contributing to raising the value of the railway lines' areas as the foundation of life in the community, and is advancing cooperation within the group to create synergies with the transportation and real estate businesses. Operating revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥511,523 million (¥507,604 million in the previous year), the largest reportable segment, accounting for just under 5 tenths of consolidated operating revenue of ¥1,086,179 million. In the retail business, structural reform is under way, and in April 2025 the company established Tokyu Retail Management Co., Ltd., which holds 6 subsidiaries that operate the company's commercial facilities such as Tokyu Department Store and Tokyu Square.
